recipes.title: Hellfoam: slip + fire + sleep (20 tiles)
recipes.tagline: Lube to drop them, napalm and phlogiston to burn them, chloral to put them down
recipes.what: Combat foam over up to 20 tiles. The foam is slippery by itself, and every tile also carries space lube, napalm, phlogiston (the igniter), chloral hydrate. A mob that stays in it for the whole 8 s life is exposed to roughly: 1.6u of lube per 0.2 s call (the floor slips for ~2 s per unit); 48u of napalm (each 0.2 s call adds about a quarter of its dose as fire stacks); 48u of phlogiston; 16u of chloral hydrate.
recipes.notes: Phlogiston ignites on ANY exposure (+1 fire stack, sets the target alight), and the napalm in the same foam turns that into a long burn. Fire heats the air and dissolves foam above 475 K, so the foam dies sooner than the full 8 s: the burn is front-loaded. The recipe makes 15u of stabilizing agent first (iron + oxygen + hydrogen). Phlogiston made WITHOUT it forms a 1000 K fireball on the borg and wipes the beaker; the engine rejects any recipe that skips it. Stabilizer in the beaker does not stop the foam. Chloral hydrate: confusion and drowsiness for the first 10 metabolism cycles, then sleep until about cycle 50 (about 100 s at 0.2u per second), then toxin damage. Fill: 100% of the beaker. All effects are cited from the reagent code, not simulated.
recipes.caution: Lethal-force chemistry: it burns, melts and puts people to sleep. Law 1 and Law 2 apply: use it only on a clear threat (an antagonist already attacking the crew), never on someone you merely suspect. Fire and acid foam also reach YOU if you stand in it: trigger it at range and stay out.
recipes.src: effects_foam.dm, reagents/toxin_reagents.dm (fluacid, napalm), drink_reagents/medicine (chloral hydrate), recipes/others.dm (phlogiston, foam)

recipes.title: Burn-mender fog (60 tiles)
recipes.tagline: Aiuri smoke, 60 tile cloud
recipes.what: Healing smoke over up to 60 tiles; each tile holds 20u aiuri (burn). Chem smoke copies a share of every reagent straight into each breathing mob in the cloud (no internals or smoke protection), so it heals people who are standing in it.
recipes.notes: Smoke gives each breathing mob up to a tile's worth of every reagent over the 20 s life; a mob that leaves early takes less. The ammonia / oil / phenol byproducts are inert (oil burns). Fill: 90%.
recipes.caution: Aiuri costs about 0.125 eye damage per second. A large dose stays in the blood a long time (0.2u per second burns off), so do not use it repeatedly on the same patient.

recipes.title: Brute-mender fog (libital smoke, 45 tiles)
recipes.tagline: Smoke that heals brute damage on everyone breathing it
recipes.what: Chem smoke copies a share of its reagents straight into every breathing mob in the cloud (no internals or smoke protection). Libital in the blood heals about 1.5 brute per second and costs about 0.15 liver damage per second; it burns off at 0.2u per second. A mob that stays the whole 20 s can absorb up to a tile's worth (30u, around 150 s of healing).
recipes.notes: Smoke is opaque and the payload is the same in every tile, so everyone in the cloud gets the same dose. The 10u of oil / 5u of phenol are inert (oil burns).
recipes.caution: The liver damage is real: do not run it repeatedly on the same patient. Dead people do not metabolise it.

recipes.title: Burn-mender fog (aiuri smoke, 45 tiles)
recipes.tagline: Smoke that heals burn damage on everyone breathing it
recipes.what: Same idea with aiuri: heals about 1 burn per second, costs about 0.125 eye damage per second, burns off at 0.2u per second. A tile holds 20u (about 100 s of healing, up to roughly 12 eye damage for someone who stands in it for the whole cloud).
recipes.notes: Hand-tuned from the planner design (which made 40u per tile) to halve the dose. The 10u of ammonia per tile is inert.
recipes.caution: Eye damage accumulates; blind or nearsighted people are the cost of a very large dose.

recipes.notes: Identical steps to metal foam; the 100u iron click stops at 60u.
recipes.caution: Same as metal foam. Sturdier walls are harder for trapped people to break out of.

recipes.title: Metal foam - instant walls (100 tiles)
recipes.tagline: Walls: seals breaches and corridors instantly (aluminium foam, 100 tiles)
recipes.what: Aluminium foam. About 8 seconds after it appears, every foam tile leaves a foamed-metal wall: dense, airtight, 20 HP, and on a space tile it also lays plating first. Seals hull breaches and corridors instantly.
recipes.notes: Needs the chem heater for the fluorosulfuric acid step. The last click is the 100u aluminium button: the dispenser stops at the free space (60u), which is exactly the 3:1 aluminium the 20u of foaming agent/acid can use. No acid is left over.
recipes.caution: Walls form on every foamed tile, including ones people stand on, so you can box people in. Never foam over injured crew or block medbay/escape routes. Bare hands bounce off the walls; any tool or weapon breaks them.

recipes.title: Black carpet foam (30 tiles)
recipes.tagline: Same but the floor becomes black carpet
ops: 1u of blood drawn with the syringe from a healthy crewmember; it is only a seed, the mutagen loop multiplies it
recipes.what: Same as carpet foam but the carpet is reacted with oil (carpet + oil -> black carpet), so every tile becomes black carpet. The carpet reagents only change a floor that is not already carpet, so the first reagent that touches a tile wins; here all the carpet has been converted so it is always black.
recipes.notes: Adds 10u each of welding fuel, carbon and hydrogen (30u oil) which eats all 30u of plain carpet.
recipes.caution: As carpet foam.

recipes.title: Carpet foam - redecorates the floor (30 tiles)
recipes.tagline: Turns the floor into carpet (cosmetic, needs a 1u blood seed)
ops: 1u of blood drawn with the syringe from a healthy crewmember; it is only a seed, the mutagen loop multiplies it
recipes.what: Carpet reagent in foam. Each foam tick turns every open solid floor tile it touches into carpet (no volume threshold). Pure cosmetics.
recipes.notes: Needs 1u of real blood as a seed. The mutagen loop (unstable mutagen + a blood catalyst -> more blood) turns dispenser chemicals into 15u of blood, which is then reacted with space drugs into 30u of carpet.
recipes.caution: Make sure the seed blood comes from a healthy person: a disease in the blood data would be copied and evolved by the loop. The foam also carries 3.2u of blood per tile.

recipes.title: Drying foam - removes lube and wet floors (30 tiles)

(The code comment says a single 5u spray is meant to clear a wet floor; every tile of this foam gets far more.)
recipes.notes: Same trigger syringe as the other foams. Planner design: 144u of drying agent per tile.
recipes.caution: The foam itself is slippery while it lasts (about 8 s), the floor is dry afterwards. Any galoshes lying in the foam are turned into dry galoshes.

recipes.title: Iron foam XL - 200 tiles (bluespace beaker)
recipes.tagline: Reinforced walls over a big area
recipes.what: Iron foam, exactly 200 tiles. About 8 seconds after it appears, every foam tile leaves a foamed-metal wall (reinforced, tougher than the aluminium walls).
recipes.notes: The metal goes in BEFORE the lithium so the reaction fires on the last click (lithium makes the foaming agent). One dispenser click is at most 100u, so putting the metal last would cap the reaction at about 165 tiles. 200 tiles is the exact fit: 40u of acid and 40u of foaming agent are all used up, so no acid ends up in the foam. A bigger 60u acid block would make 235 tiles but leaves 13u of acid in the foam. The last click is the 100u lithium button: the dispenser stops at the free space (40u), exactly what the 40u of hydrogen can turn into foaming agent. 60u of the metal is left over and harmless.
recipes.caution: Walls form on every foamed tile, including ones people stand on, so you can box people in. Never foam over injured crew or block medbay/escape routes. Bare hands bounce off the walls; any tool or weapon breaks them.

recipes.tagline: Walls only on area borders / breach rims, plates over space
recipes.what: Smart foam only leaves a wall on a tile that touches a different area (door frames, hull edges, breach rims) and plates over space. You can flood a whole room and only its perimeter gets sealed.
recipes.notes: The smart foaming agent has to be made before aluminium goes in, otherwise plain foaming agent + acid + aluminium fires ordinary metal foam. Needs a bluespace beaker for the room (the intermediates plus the 100u aluminium click do not fit a 100u beaker).
recipes.caution: The leftover oil and acetone in the foam is inert but oil burns.

recipes.notes: Needs both upgrades: the bluespace syringe holds 60u of trigger, and 60 surfactant + 60 water + 31 payload + the injected 60 only fit a big beaker.

recipes.title: Friendly life (bluespace beaker, donated ingredients)
recipes.tagline: Spawns 1 to 3 random friendly mobs (needs donated ingredients)
recipes.what: Strange reagent + synthflesh + sugar at 374 K or more spawns random friendly mobs (neutral faction): rand(1, mult) of them, with a flash for everyone who can see it. Each 30u of each ingredient is one mult, so a 300u beaker (270u of ingredients) allows mult 3 -> 1 to 3 mobs.
recipes.notes: The donors are the catch: strange reagent (omnizine + holy water + unstable mutagen) and synthflesh (blood + carbon + libital) are not dispenser reagents in a normal round. Sugar comes from the dispenser. This entry only shows the bigger-beaker maths.
recipes.caution: The mobs are picked at random from the same friendly list the gold slime extract uses (every simple/basic animal flagged friendly-spawnable); they can still make a mess.

recipes.title: Dark matter pull - drags everything toward you (range 6)
recipes.tagline: Pulls everything within 6 tiles toward you
recipes.what: Liquid dark matter is the mirror image: the same vortex, but things are pulled toward the beaker. Good for gathering scattered items or a crowd into one spot.
recipes.notes: Range is clamp(sqrt(3 x mult), 1, 6): mult 12 is enough for the cap, 15u of each ingredient gives mult 15. The last click fires it.
recipes.caution: Pulled/thrown mobs can be hurt by the landing. Do not use it on crew.

recipes.title: Sorium shockwave - throws everything away from you (range 6)
recipes.tagline: Throws everything within 6 tiles away from you
recipes.what: Sorium makes a vortex around the beaker: everything unanchored within the range (items and living mobs, not corpses) is thrown away from the centre. Targets closer than range-2 tiles are thrown (power range-distance), farther ones get one or two steps. You (the centre tile) are not moved.
recipes.notes: Four clicks, the last one fires it. The range is clamp(sqrt(4 x mult), 1, 6), so mult 9 already reaches the 6 tile cap: more reagent is wasted, a bigger beaker does not help. Stabilizing agent in the beaker cancels it.
recipes.caution: People thrown into walls are injured. Only for scattering hostile mobs or clearing an item pile; Law 1 applies to everyone else in range.
